To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a new robust subspace tracking algorithm based on the APSM method is proposed, 2) a sparsity promoting greedy algorithm is employed to detect outliers in the observation vectors and 3) a new prediction scheme is developed for the estimation of the missing entries of the observation vectors.

we introduce a new algorithm for robust subsphere estimation, that we introduce a novel approach for the problem of robust matrix completion, that we provide a theoretical analysis of our algorithm and that we demonstrate its superiority in terms of performance compared to the state of the art.

we propose a novel algorithm for robust subsparse subspace tracking, that is, a method for estimating the subspace of a data set, where some of the data points may be outliers and the algorithm can be used in cases when the data are partially observed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of algorithms for robust estimation of low-rank matrices, with missing entries, in the presence of outliers.
the problem of robust subspace tracking in the presence of outlier noise and missing entries.
the development of robust subspace tracking methods for applications, where the observation vectors may be contaminated by outliers and/or may be partially observed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this is a novel and robust approach for subspace tracking, which has a very wide range of applications in the fields of signal processing and machine learning, such as robust principal component analysis, robust subspace identification, and robust low-rank matrix recovery, to mention a few.

the APSM algorithm is able to track the subspace of interest in the presence of outliers and missing entries, with high accuracy, while the computational burden is low, compared to the state of the art.
the proposed APSM-based algorithm is a powerful and efficient method, which can be used in many applications, where the data are contaminated with outliers and the data are partially observed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed algorithm can track an unknown subspace in the presence of outliers and missing entries, with a low computational complexity and with no need for a priori knowledge of the number of outliers or the number of missing entries.
we introduce an adaptive algorithm for robust subspectral tracking and robust matrix completion.

the proposed APSM-based scheme is capable of robustly tracking the subspace spanned by the data vectors, even if the latter contain outliers, as well as missing entries, and is capable to achieve this goal in a computationally efficient way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed scheme is able to track the underlying subspace even in the presence of heavy outlier noise and missing observations.
the proposed APSM algorithm is capable of handling the case of missing entries in a robust manner, without the need for any prior knowledge of the number and location of these entries.

a proper combination of sparsity-promoting techniques and set-theoretic optimization tools, can lead to a robust and efficient solution to the subspace tracking problem, with or without the presence of outlier noise and with or without missing data entries.
